name: Content Analyzer
description: Structural fact extraction from scraped content. Classifies into categories (fixed taxonomy), assigns tags, extracts key facts (people, licenses, awards, partnerships, offices, contact), and maps source citations. No summaries, opinions, or marketing prose — pure classification and extraction.
usage_notes: MODEL FLOOR — haiku-4-5 is BELOW this module's capability floor. It reads its reference taxonomy doc (master_categories.md) but does NOT comply with it: it fabricates categories instead of assigning from the configured list. Tested 2026-06, reproduced 100% of tries; escalating to sonnet resolves it. MINIMUM MODEL: sonnet. Any template assigning haiku to content-analyzer is misconfigured. (The v1.4.1 vocabulary-fidelity gate loud-fails such entities only when `vocabulary_checks` is configured; the model floor holds regardless of that gate.) max_tokens RECONCILIATION: because the floor is sonnet — a Claude-5 model with adaptive thinking ON by default — the manifest default of 16384 is UNDER-PROVISIONED here. 16384 was sized for haiku (no thinking overhead); sonnet's thinking consumes the budget invisibly, so 16384 can truncate and the skeleton fail-closed guard turns truncation into a run failure. A sonnet template MUST override max_tokens to 32768. The 16384 default (and the 'sized for haiku' wording on the max_tokens/ai_model option descriptions) are legacy haiku-era values, NOT the intended operating point — do not read them as current. Increase max_content_chars for entities with extensive source material (50+ scraped pages). Runs independently of seo-planner. CONTENT GATE (v1.4.3, M2): after the analysis parses, content-analyzer asserts it carries at least one usable extracted value; a valid-but-empty (HOLLOW) analysis fails LOUD with meta.status:'error' (entity turns red) instead of shipping an empty analysis as success — content-writer and seo-planner both serialize the whole analysis_json into their prompt, so a hollow analysis would cascade into a hollow profile. A non-JSON response keeps its existing raw-text path (out of scope). See README. B029 (v1.6.0, template-v3 unit): (1) `include_page_intent` default-off — ON gives per-page url/title/intent headers in the assembled prompt (framing B, ~25 tok/page); v3 flips it true; requires_columns now hydrates page_intent/intent_confidence for it. (2) input-truncation visibility, always-on additive — when the assembled source exceeds max_content_chars the result item and meta carry content_truncated/content_chars_total/content_chars_kept (plus a logged warning); prompt bytes unchanged. (3) `json_retry` default-off — ON ports seo-planner's v2.2.1 corrective JSON retry (one temperature-0 re-ask, cache_prefix stripped) and FAILS the entity loud on a second non-JSON response instead of the degraded raw-text success; v3 flips it true so a garbage analysis halts at step 5 rather than reaching the writer. SOURCE-CHECK GATE (v1.7.0, `source_check` default OFF = byte-identical): deterministic, $0, no LLM call. For every fact carrying a `source` URL (recursive walk — no schema path hardcoded), verifies a currency+amount the fact asserts against the FULL text of the page that fact cites (the module's own `items` text_content): if a magnitude-bearing amount (m/bn/k — bare-number amounts like £5 are skipped to stay false-positive safe) appears on the cited page but the claimed currency is NOT adjacent to it (±25 chars), the whole element is removed — a currency SUBSTITUTION. Removals are recorded on meta.source_check (counts + per-violation {path,source,kind,field,reason}); nothing is dropped silently, and removed facts never reach the writer/draft. VALIDATED on the six real run-9821ed56 analyses (855 cited facts): fired once — the genuine BC '£50m' where the cited page says €50m — with ZERO false positives, including on the three re-audit REFUTED cases. SCOPE — this is currency cite-or-null ONLY. The re-audit's other genuine defects were each tested against the real analyses and deliberately LEFT OUT because they would null legitimate facts: (a) DATE cite-or-null (BC PariuriX '2016' on an undated page) — built then removed on evidence: 'cited page lacks the asserted year' fired on 18 real facts, 1 genuine + 17 world-TRUE dates whose cited page carries no year in scraped form (Step-3 scrapers strip publication dates — DEFECT_REAUDIT §5; date lives in URL path / news-index / stripped dateline). 'Year absent' cannot deterministically separate a world-false uncited date from a world-true one, so it would null 17 legitimate dates; FP-safe date checking needs the scraper to preserve publication dates first (data-layer, out of scope). (b) Push Dinopolis award-CATEGORY, BC Søgaard person→company, PayRetailers Kuady relation — in each the named subject IS present on the cited page, only the claim/attribution is wrong; catching them needs fuzzy claim-phrase or cross-page attribution matching that re-introduces the FP class the re-audit exists to kill. A named-subject-presence check was built and rejected because on `name` fields it false-positives the refuted Vixio Woolfrey '(former)'. All route to human review, not blind patching. Re-audit: content-pipeline-specs template-v3/quality/DEFECT_REAUDIT.md, 2026-09-19.

options.name: ai_model
options.label: AI Model
options.description: Which model to use for content analysis. Haiku is fast and cheap for structured extraction.

options.name: reference_docs
options.label: Reference Documents
options.description: Reference docs for the analysis prompt. Key docs: master_categories.md (fixed taxonomy), master_tags.md (tag list). Upload once, reuse across runs.

options.name: temperature
options.label: Temperature
options.description: LLM temperature for analysis. Lower = more consistent extraction. Default 0.2 for reliable structured output.

options.name: max_tokens
options.label: Max output tokens
options.description: Maximum tokens in the LLM response. Sized for haiku (no thinking overhead); complete analyses on 200+ page inputs run 1.2k-6.6k tokens. If you switch this module to a Claude-5 model (sonnet/opus), adaptive thinking consumes this budget invisibly — raise it or truncation fails the run.

options.name: max_content_chars
options.label: Max content characters
options.description: Truncate assembled source text to this many characters to control token usage.

options.name: include_page_intent
options.label: Include page intent in framing
options.description: B029-1 (v1.6.0, default false = byte-identical legacy framing). When true, each page in the assembled prompt gets a numbered header with url/title lines plus the page's Step-2 intent classification (`intent: {page_intent} (confidence {intent_confidence})`; line omitted when the item has no page_intent). ~25 extra tokens per page. Intended ON for the v3 template.

options.name: json_retry
options.label: Corrective JSON retry (fail-loud)
options.description: B029-3 (v1.6.0, default false = legacy behavior: a non-JSON LLM response becomes a degraded success with raw text in section_analysis). When true, a non-JSON response triggers ONE temperature-0 corrective re-ask embedding the invalid response (seo-planner v2.2.1 pattern, cache_prefix stripped); if that also fails to parse, the entity FAILS loud (meta.status 'error', analysis_json null) instead of shipping prose downstream. Intended ON for the v3 template.

options.name: source_check
options.label: Source-check gate (currency cite-or-null)
options.description: v1.7.0, default false = byte-identical (gate inert). When true, after analysis each extracted fact carrying a `source` URL is verified against the full text of the page it cites (the module's own scraped items — deterministic, no LLM call, $0): a currency amount whose claimed currency is not adjacent to that amount on the cited page (a currency substitution, e.g. the fact says £50m but the page says €50m) has its whole fact removed so it never reaches the writer; every removal is recorded on meta.source_check for review. Scoped to currency cite-or-null only — validated 0 false positives on the six banked run-9821ed56 analyses (855 facts). Does NOT check dates (scrapers strip publication dates, so 'cited page lacks the year' would null legitimate dates) or subject/attribution/relation welds (those route to human review). Pipeline-agnostic: keyed only on the generic `source` URL, no schema path or content-type knowledge.

options.name: vocabulary_checks
options.label: Vocabulary fidelity checks (per-template)
options.description:
Optional, pipeline-agnostic. When set, after analysis the writer validates that every slug assigned at the given analysis_json path exists in the named reference doc (the injected vocabulary). An assigned slug not found in that doc FAILS the entity, and a missing/empty referenced doc fails the run before any LLM call. Leave EMPTY for content types that do not enforce a closed vocabulary — the gate is then inert.

Format: one entry per line, `<analysis_json.path[].slug>=<reference_doc_name>`. The path uses the same `field.subfield[].leaf` walk as content-writer's allowed_slug_paths. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored.

Example for a company-profile pipeline:
    categories.primary[].slug=master_categories.md
    categories.secondary[].slug=master_categories.md
    tags.existing[].slug=master_tags.md

options.name: prompt
options.label: Analysis prompt
options.description: The prompt sent to the AI. Use {entity_content} for scraped content, {doc:master_categories.md} and {doc:master_tags.md} for taxonomy lists, {doc:filename} for other reference docs.
